nodes.title: Keep the state in the children only
nodes.why: Each child carries its own checked flag, and the parent stores nothing. The parent can then never disagree with the children, because everything it shows is read from them.
nodes.alternative: Give the parent its own checked and indeterminate refs and update them from every handler.
nodes.tradeoff: Separate refs need a sync step after every change and drift when one is missed; deriving costs a count over three children on each change.

nodes.title: Count the checked children once
nodes.why: Both parent states depend on how many children are checked. One computed counts them and caches the number until a flag changes.
nodes.alternative: Count inside each computed or in the template.
nodes.tradeoff: Repeating the count is harmless for three children, but a shared computed keeps the rule in one place.

nodes.title: Make the parent a writable computed
nodes.why: v-model on the parent checkbox reads the getter for checked and calls the setter on a click, so one binding covers both directions without a change handler.
nodes.alternative: Bind :checked to a read-only computed and handle @change to set the children.
nodes.tradeoff: The handler version is just as valid and shows the event explicitly; the writable computed keeps reading and writing next to each other.

nodes.title: Write every child in place
nodes.why: Vue tracks changes made in place on reactive objects, so assigning each child flag updates the children, the count and the parent in one pass. From a mixed state the browser reports the click as checked, so every child becomes checked.
nodes.alternative: Build a new array of copied children and assign it to children.value.
nodes.tradeoff: A new array is tracked as well; in Vue it is a style choice, not something reactivity needs.

nodes.title: Derive the mixed state for :indeterminate
nodes.why: indeterminate exists only as a DOM property. The template binds :indeterminate="someChecked", and Vue sets the property, so no template ref is needed.
nodes.alternative: Keep a template ref on the parent input and assign el.indeterminate in a watcher.
nodes.tradeoff: The ref and watcher work too, but they duplicate what the binding does and add a step that can run late.
